description: Alamo Group Inc. manufactures and sells industrial and vegetation management equipment for governmental, industrial, and agricultural uses worldwide. It operates in two segments, Vegetation Management
description_full: Alamo Group Inc. manufactures and sells industrial and vegetation management equipment for governmental, industrial, and agricultural uses worldwide. It operates in two segments, Vegetation Management and Industrial Equipment. The Vegetation Management segment offers tractor powered equipment such as rotary, finishing, flail, and disc mowers; rotary cutters; front end loaders, backhoes, tillers, posthole diggers, scraper blades, cultivators, subsoilers, and other tractor attachments and implements. This segment also provides commercial and residential zero turn mowers; hydraulic and mechanical boom and reach mowers; hedge and hedgerow cutters; industrial grass mowers; seedbed preparation equipment; and forestry and tree care tools, including chippers, stump grinders, mulchers, brush cutters, flails, and debarkers, as well as remote control mowers and related replacement parts. Its Industrial Equipment segment offers hydraulic telescoping booms; catch basin and roadway debris vacuum systems; sewer cleaners; vacuum trucks, combination sewer cleaners, hydro excavators, trenchers, and high pressure cleaning systems; truck mounted snow plows, blowers, dump bodies, spreaders, deicers, brine sprayers, snow throwers, and wing systems; salt spreaders; street sweepers, including mechanical broom and regenerative air models; leaf and debris collection equipment and replacement brooms; solid waste and recycling equipment; municipal tractors and attachments; asphalt patchers; underground construction forms; traffic control and crash attenuator trucks; industrial vacuum excavation units; trailer mounted and custom truck mounted systems; and related accessories and truck up fitting services. The company serves the infrastructure building and maintenance, industrial construction, public works, land maintenance, agriculture, and tree care markets. Alamo Group Inc. was founded in 1955 and is headquartered in Seguin, Texas.

financial_summary: Alamo Group, Inc. is a small-cap industrials business with a $1.7B market cap on $1.6B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +2% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 12% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 25% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $147M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.71× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 10.2×.
Shareholder yield is only 0.9%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

sect: Its 9% operating margin is roughly in line with the Industrials median (9%).
It earns less of the sector's profit than its revenue share would suggest (0.85x).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-1.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 548 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted lower, down 6% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 37% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 33% and a beta of 0.89, it moves roughly with the market.
About $25.7M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 42% in the 2020 crash, 31% in the 2022 bear market and 64% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $132 (margin of safety -5%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 26%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $111 to $160 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Industrials peers: EV/EBITDA 10.1 vs 13.4 and P/FCF 11.5 vs 22.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 16% below its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are attractive: an FCF yield of 8.7% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 8.8% (vs the 8% bar).
The 4 covering analysts target $184 on average, 32% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 12% earns above the cost of capital of 8.8%, but the 3pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.18).
It runs a 25% gross margin and converts 9% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.71x.
ROE of 9% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.4x equity multiplier).
It spends 0.6% of revenue on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $118.9M (7% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 5.0, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 141 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 1.9% over 3 years, 6.6% over 5 years and 6.2% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating.
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 11.6% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -2.5% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.1x, 1.9% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 15, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.2%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insider trading is two-way: 1 purchase and 4 sales over the past year, net $1.0M sold.
Shareholder yield is a modest 0.9% (0.1% in buybacks and 1.0% in dividends).
It has paid a dividend for 32 consecutive years, raising it 18.7% a year over the last five.
people: With about 3,800 employees, each generates about $422K of revenue, 1.2x the Industrials median, and revenue has grown 7.2% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $39K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $983K (2x revenue per employee).
